verdicts.summary: A steered question notice is lost for good if the parent's provider turn ends as failed or interrupted (not completed) before the steer effect delivers it. The note's failure_mode only covers the turnCompleted race. Before this change the notice stayed a queued run behind the parent turn, so it survived this case.
verdicts.scenario: 1) A background task (completionWake 'always') opens a pending user_input request while the parent run is running on a provider that can steer. 2) The reactor dispatches the notice. Orchestrator.ts:5766-5772 upgrades it to steer_active, and dispatchSteerIntoRun attaches the message and the notification card to the running run (4961-4967) and queues a provider-turn.steer effect (4968-4982). 3) Before the worker runs that effect, the parent provider turn moves to 'failed' (provider error) or 'interrupted' (Stop lands after the dispatch-time stopReachedRun check). 4) ProviderTurnControlService.ts:136-144 fails with turnCompleted=false. EffectWorker.ts:265-270 rethrows, so no follow-up is dispatched. 5) Nothing delivers it again. The mailbox redelivery path covers delegatedCompletion only (EffectWorker.ts:254, NotificationMailbox.ts:25). A later wake by the reactor reuses commandId `server:delegated-task-question:${key}` (DelegatedTaskQuestionReactor.ts:45), and the receipt dedup at Orchestrator.ts:13462 turns it into a no-op.
verdicts.consequence: The parent thread shows a 'has a question' notification card, but the parent agent never received the text. A blocking child question then stays pending with no agent wake and no queued run to resume. Before this change the notice was a queued (possibly held) run that ran after the failed turn.

verdicts.summary: In the turnCompleted case, the queued retry puts the existing message on a new queued run under the same message id. The reactor's cancel-on-answer path still finds that run, and receipts dedupe repeats. The model-selection difference is already finding 0.
verdicts.scenario: The steer loses the race (turn completed). The retry re-dispatches the message as queue_after_active, passing its notification. Then the child's question is answered before the queued run starts. The reactor looks for a queued run whose userMessageId equals the notice's message id and cancels it. The queued path writes the message with id=command.messageId and runId set to the new run, so the lookup matches and the run is cancelled. Retrying the same effect again reuses commandId steer-follow-up:${effect.id}, which the receipt dedupes.
